chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon you is with the advising among His creatures, for you will never meet Him with a deed more superior than it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'al-nush' (sincere counsel) as the paramount deed for attaining divine proximity, elevating it above other acts of worship. This concept, central to Shia ethical theology, underscores that true piety is manifested through selfless service to God's creation, reflecting the principle that serving the creatures is a means to serving the Creator. The emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) ensures that the act is not merely social advice but a spiritual practice that purifies the soul and strengthens communal bonds.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Upon you is with the advising among His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, for you will never (be able to) meet Him<sup>azwj</sup> with a deed more superior than it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyayna who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘You must, for the sake of Allah, offer good advice to His creatures; you will not meet Him with any deed better than this.’”
